title: Automation of Bio-Atomic Force Microscope Measurements on Hundreds of C. albicans Cells
protocol: Revivify C. albicans cells from a glycerol stock stored at -80°C.
Rub a marble containing C. albicans on YPD agar and grow for 2 days at 30°C.
Prepare liquid cultures by filling a culture tube with 5 mL of sterile YPD broth and adding a single colony of C. albicans cells grown on the YPD agar plate.
Grow the culture in static conditions at 30°C for 20 hours before harvesting by centrifugation (4000 x g, 5 min).
Discard the supernatant and eliminate as biohazard waste.
Wash the pellets twice with 10 mL of acetate buffer (8 mM sodium acetate, 1 mM CaCl₂, 1 mM MnCl₂, pH 5.2), centrifuging at 4000 x g for 5 minutes between washes.
Resuspend the pellet in 2 mL of acetate buffer and use this solution for cell immobilization on the PDMS stamp.
Draw the desired microstructures using computer-assisted design (CAD) software to prepare a silicon master mold.
Prepare 55 g of PDMS prepolymer solution containing a mixture of 10 to 1, mass ratio, of PDMS oligomers and curing agent.
Mix and degas this solution under vacuum until all trapped bubbles are removed (5−10 min).
Pour 20 g of the degassed solution on the silicon master mold.
Degas again under vacuum.
Reticulate the PDMS at 80 °C for 1 hour.
Cut the PDMS microstructured stamp with a scalpel (0.5 x 1.5 cm²) parallel to the visible microstructure arrays.
Peel the stamp from the silicon master mold.
Deposit the stamp on a glass slide with the microstructures facing up.
Align the microstructures that can be seen on the stamp with the side of the glass slide for later reference in AFM automation procedure.
Centrifuge 600 μL of the resuspended cell solution at 500 x g for 5 min to separate buffer from cells.
Pipette 200 μL of the supernatant onto the PDMS stamp.
Degas the stamp under vacuum in the range of 10-1-10-2 bars for about 40 min.
Remove the buffer from the PDMS surface with a pipette.
Deposit 200 μL of the cell solution onto the PDMS surface for 15 min at room temperature.
Place cells into microstructures of the stamp by convective/capillary assembly.
Spread 200 μL of cell suspension across the stamp using a glass slide in both directions with an angle between 30 and 50°.
Remove the cell suspension with a pipette.
Wash the stamp 3x with 1 mL of acetate buffer, pH 5.2 to remove cells that were not trapped.
Dry the back of the stamp using nitrogen flow.
Deposit the PDMS stamp filled with cells in a Petri dish and fill it with 2 mL of acetate buffer.
Place the Petri dish with the stamp in the AFM Petri dish holder, aligning the stamp edge perpendicular to the Petri dish holder Y axis.
Place the AFM head onto the stage carefully to avoid crashing on the stamp.
Center the stage at 0:0 when starting AFM operations.
Calibrate sensitivity and spring constant of the cantilever on glass and in water.
Center the AFM tip on the top left corner of the 4.5 x 4.5 µm² wells.
Perform a 64 x 64 force map over a 100 x 100 µm² area with Z range = 4 µm, tip velocity = 90 µm·s-1, and applied force of 3 to 5 nN.
Select Force Mapping mode from the Measurement mode drop-down box.
Input Rel. Setpoint = 3 to 5 nN in the force control mapping panel.
Set z length to 4 µm; Z movement: constant duration; extend time: 0.01s; ext. delay: 0; retraction delay: 0, Delay mode: Constant Force, Sample rate 2048 Hz.
Uncheck Z closed loop in the force control mapping panel.
Check Square image and set Fast to 100 µm, slow to 100µm; X offset: 0 µm; Y offset: 0 µm; grid angle: 0 degree; Pixels: 64x64; pixel ratio: 1:1.
Note the coordinates of the center of the top left well (W1) and of the bottom left well (referred as W2).
Open the automation software (Automatip_scan.py): in the JPK desktop software click on advance in the top bar menu and select open the script.
Select the path toward the script file provided in Supplementary Data (Automatip_scan.py).
Implement W1 and W2 coordinate values in the Inputs box section of the Jython script.
Input the W1 coordinates in the P1 variable line 239 of the script.
Input the W2 coordinates in the P2 variable line 241 of the script.
Attribute the pitch value to the pitch variable line 245 of the script.
Input the well dimension in the Ws variable line 248 of the script.
Write the path to the saving directory in line 251 to save the data at the desired place.
Set the totalArea variable line 254 to the desired multiple "n" of 100 µm.
Set the force curves matrix, row and column (3, 3 or 4, 4), recorded per well in the numScans variable line 257.
Run the program.
Click on the Start button.
Execute a centering algorithm to determine the center of W1 and W2 wells automatically (step 1).
Acquire the Force Curves matrix on each well of the first scanning area (step 2).
Move the AFM tip to the first well of the next scanning area after all wells in the current area are probed.
Retract the tip, move the microscope stage to the next area, and re-approach the tip onto the stamp.
Execute a centering algorithm again on the first well of the new area (step 3).
Define subsequent areas as right of previous areas until n is reached. Continue with n+1 underneath n, n+2 left of n+1, etc., up to 2n.
Proceed with 2n+1 underneath 2n and 2n+2 right of 2n.
Repeat steps 2 and 3 automatically for the total number "n2" of scanning areas.
Execute the "Copy_files" python script (Copy_files_L.py) to organize the FCs files into one folder.
Input path to the general folder in line 67 of the script provided in supplementary data.
Input where it will be stored in line 73 of the script provided in supplementary data.
Open the AFM manufacturer data processing software to analyze the force curves.
In the top menu File, select open ‘batch of spectroscopy curves’.
In the batch processing window, select the process provided in Supplementary Data (StiffnessProcess.jpk-proc-force).
Select the last step of the process and click on Keep and Apply to All.
Repeat steps 4.2.1 to 4.2.3 for all experiments.
Save data in different folders based on treatment status (e.g., “...TREATED\” and “...UNTREATED\”).
Open the R script DataAnalisys.R using R studio software.
Load .tsv files containing extracted information from data processing software.
In the environment window, use the Import Dataset button.
From the list displayed, select "from text (readr)".
Select the Browser button to find and load the .tsv file.
Once loaded, select columns for stiffness and adhesion analysis.
Run all code in the script by pressing Ctrl+Alt+R.
